hook: The prince of Wallachia whose cruelty gave the world Dracula.

pages.x: Vlad was born around 1431, son of Vlad Dracul, prince of Wallachia, in what is now Romania. "Dracul" came from the Order of the Dragon his father had joined, so Vlad was "Dracula", son of the dragon. As a boy he and his brother were sent as hostages to the Ottoman sultan.

His father and elder brother were murdered by rebel nobles; his brother was buried alive. Vlad won the throne for good in 1456 and, the stories say, invited the nobles to a feast and had them impaled on stakes.

He ruled through terror. A story says he left a golden cup by a fountain for anyone to drink from, and no one ever dared steal it. Thieves, liars and enemies were impaled. German pamphlets with woodcuts of him dining among the dead became early best-sellers.

In 1462 Sultan Mehmed II invaded with a huge army. Vlad burned crops and poisoned wells, then led a night raid on the Ottoman camp, trying to kill the sultan himself. Marching on, the Ottomans found a forest of thousands of impaled prisoners outside his capital, and turned back.
Betrayed, he spent years as a prisoner of the king of Hungary. He won back his throne in 1476 but was killed in battle within months, and his head was sent to Constantinople.

In 1897 the Irish writer Bram Stoker borrowed the name Dracula for the vampire count of his novel. Vlad never drank blood, but Bran Castle, which has little to do with him, now draws crowds of tourists as "Dracula's castle".
In Romania, Vlad is remembered as a hero who fought the Ottomans and punished corrupt nobles. Elsewhere, his cruelty and his name made him the model for the most famous vampire in fiction.
